title: A request to travel
summary: After a church has been established in the land, Lamoni desires Ammon to accompany him to the land of Nephi. The Lord tells Ammon not to go there, but to go to Middoni, where Aaron, Muloki, and Ammah are imprisoned.

explicit_facts.text: A church had been established in the land, and Lamoni desired Ammon to go with him to the land of Nephi.
The Lord told Ammon not to go to the land of Nephi, but to go to Middoni because Aaron, Muloki, and Ammah were imprisoned there.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord's message can be conveyed as off-screen speech; no visible divine appearance is described.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the Lord, if any; the setting's precise appearance; whether Lamoni and Ammon are together when the voice comes.

spoken_dialogue.text: Thou shalt not go up to the land of Nephi,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Aaron, Muloki, or Ammah in prison in this scene; their imprisonment is reported, not shown.

title: Ammon tells Lamoni
summary: Ammon tells Lamoni that his brother and brethren are imprisoned in Middoni and that he intends to deliver them. Lamoni says he will go with Ammon and plead with Middoni's king. He asks who told Ammon about the imprisonment; Ammon answers that God did.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon told Lamoni that his brother and brethren were imprisoned in Middoni and that he was going to deliver them.
Lamoni said he would accompany Ammon to Middoni and plead with its king, Antiomno, who was Lamoni's friend.
Lamoni asked who had told Ammon that his brethren were imprisoned; Ammon said God had told him.

unspecified_visual_details: The precise setting and the characters' appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, my brother and brethren are in prison at Middoni, and I go that I may deliver them.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon (son of Mosiah)

spoken_dialogue.text: Who told thee that thy brethren were in prison?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Lamoni

spoken_dialogue.text: No one hath told me, save it be God;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon (son of Mosiah)

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Antiomno; he is mentioned but is not present in the described conversation.

title: Preparing to depart
summary: Lamoni has his servants prepare horses and chariots, then tells Ammon to go with him to Middoni, where he will plead for the release of Ammon's brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni caused his servants to prepare his horses and chariots.
Lamoni said he would accompany Ammon to Middoni and plead for his brethren to be released from prison.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Servants preparing horses and chariots may be shown as the immediate action.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and appearance of horses, chariots, and servants; the precise setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: Come, I will go with thee down to the land of Middoni,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Lamoni

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the journey beginning in this scene; it is described in the following verses.

title: Meeting Lamoni's father
summary: While journeying, Ammon and Lamoni meet Lamoni's father, king over all the land. He asks Lamoni why he did not come to the feast and where he is going with Ammon, whom he calls one of the children of a liar.
characters: Lamoni's father (king over all the land)

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and Lamoni met Lamoni's father while journeying.
Lamoni's father was king over all the land.
Lamoni's father asked why Lamoni had not come to the feast he made for his sons and people.
Lamoni's father asked where Lamoni was going with the Nephite, whom he called one of the children of a liar.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The three can be shown together at the moment they meet during the journey.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain, clothing, and characters' appearances are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Why did ye not come to the feast on that great day when I made a feast unto my sons, and unto my people?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lamoni's father

spoken_dialogue.text: Whither art thou going with this Nephite, who is one of the children of a liar?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lamoni's father

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier feast as part of this meeting.

title: Lamoni explains
summary: Lamoni explains to his father where he is going and why he had stayed in his own kingdom instead of attending the feast.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni told his father where he was going because he feared to offend him.
Lamoni told his father why he had stayed in his own kingdom instead of going to the feast.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamoni is speaking to his father during their meeting on the journey.
unspecified_visual_details: Lamoni's exact words, since they are summarized rather than quoted; the setting's precise appearance.

title: The father becomes angry
summary: Lamoni's father becomes angry after hearing his explanation. He accuses Ammon and the Nephites of deception and commands Lamoni to kill Ammon and return with him to Ishmael, not Middoni.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni's father became angry and accused the Nephites of being liars who sought to deceive and rob his people.
He commanded Lamoni to slay Ammon and to return with him to Ishmael rather than go to Middoni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon is present during the confrontation, as the father commands Lamoni to kill him.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the sword is drawn yet; the precise setting and characters' appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lamoni, thou art going to deliver these Nephites, who are sons of a liar.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Lamoni attacking Ammon; no such action occurs.

title: Lamoni refuses
summary: Lamoni refuses to kill Ammon or return to Ishmael, and says he will go to Middoni to release Ammon's brethren. His father grows angry and draws his sword to strike Lamoni.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni refused to kill Ammon or return to Ishmael; he said he would go to Middoni to release Ammon's brethren, whom he knew to be just and holy prophets of the true God.
Lamoni's father became angry and drew his sword to strike Lamoni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The drawn sword may be shown as the father prepares to strike Lamoni; do not show an injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The sword's design and the precise setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will not slay Ammon, neither will I return to the land of Ishmael,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Lamoni

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a blow landing or Lamoni being injured.

title: Ammon intervenes
summary: Ammon steps forward and warns Lamoni's father not to kill his son. He urges the king to refrain, warning that killing Lamoni would bring consequences and might cost the king his soul.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: Ammon stood forth and told Lamoni's father not to kill his son; he said Lamoni had repented and warned the king about acting in anger.
Ammon urged the king to refrain, warning that Lamoni was innocent and that killing him could bring vengeance and cause the king to lose his soul.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon steps into the confrontation while the king has drawn his sword.
unspecified_visual_details: Ammon's precise gesture and the characters' expressions.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, thou shalt not slay thy son;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon (son of Mosiah)

spoken_dialogue.text: And again, it is expedient that thou shouldst forbear;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon (son of Mosiah)

prohibited_inventions: The reference to blood crying from the ground is figurative teaching, not a visible supernatural event.

title: The king turns on Ammon
summary: Lamoni's father acknowledges that killing his son would shed innocent blood, but says Ammon sought to destroy him. He reaches to kill Ammon; Ammon withstands his blows and strikes the king's arm so he cannot use it.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: Lamoni's father said that killing his son would shed innocent blood and accused Ammon of seeking to destroy him.
The king stretched out his hand to kill Ammon. Ammon withstood his blows and struck the king's arm so he could not use it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The explicitly described physical struggle may be shown without depicting wounds, blood, or severed body parts.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact movements and the appearance of the setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: I know that if I should slay my son, that I should shed innocent blood;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

prohibited_inventions: Do not add gore or depict a wound.

title: The king pleads for his life
summary: Seeing that Ammon could kill him, the king pleads for his life. Ammon raises his sword and demands the release of his brethren. The king promises to grant whatever Ammon asks, even half the kingdom, if Ammon spares him.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: The king saw that Ammon could kill him and pleaded that Ammon spare his life.
Ammon raised his sword and demanded that his brethren be released from prison.
The king offered to grant whatever Ammon asked, even half the kingdom, if Ammon spared him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon's raised sword and the king's plea may be shown as the same continuous standoff.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise posture of the king and Lamoni; the sword's design.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I will smite thee except thou wilt grant unto me that my brethren may be cast out of prison.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon (son of Mosiah)

spoken_dialogue.text: If thou wilt spare me I will grant unto thee whatsoever thou wilt ask, even to half of the kingdom.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Ammon striking the king in this moment.

title: Ammon states his conditions
summary: Ammon asks the king to release his brethren, allow Lamoni to retain his kingdom, and let Lamoni act according to his own desires. Ammon promises to spare the king if he agrees; the king begins to rejoice at the prospect of living.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: Ammon conditioned sparing the king on the release of his brethren, Lamoni retaining his kingdom, and the king not displeasing Lamoni or restricting his choices.
The king began to rejoice because of his life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king's relief may be shown in his expression or posture.
unspecified_visual_details: The characters' precise expressions, gestures, and the setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: If thou wilt grant that my brethren may be cast out of prison, and also that Lamoni may retain his kingdom,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ammon (son of Mosiah)

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the king's agreement before his words in the next verses.

title: The king agrees
summary: The king, astonished by Ammon's love for Lamoni, agrees that Lamoni may retain his kingdom and that he will no longer govern him. He also agrees to release Ammon's brethren and invites Ammon and them to visit him in his kingdom.
characters: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

explicit_facts.text: The king was astonished by Ammon's desire to spare him and his love for Lamoni.
The king agreed that Lamoni could retain his kingdom and that he would govern him no more.
The king agreed to have Ammon's brethren released and invited Ammon and his brethren to visit him in his kingdom; he desired to learn from their words.

unspecified_visual_details: The exact staging and expressions during the agreement.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will grant unto you that my son may retain his kingdom from this time and forever;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

spoken_dialogue.text: And I will also grant unto thee that thy brethren may be cast out of prison,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The king over all the land (Lamoni's father)

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the prisoners being released yet; that occurs after the journey to Middoni.

title: Journey to Middoni
summary: Ammon and Lamoni continue their journey to Middoni. Lamoni finds favor with Middoni's king, and Ammon's brethren are brought out of prison.
characters: The king of the land of Middoni

explicit_facts.text: Ammon and Lamoni continued their journey toward Middoni.
Lamoni found favor with Middoni's king, and Ammon's brethren were brought out of prison.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Middoni's king, the prison, and the route of travel.

title: Ammon Meets the Afflicted People
summary: Ammon meets them and is exceedingly sorrowful. They are naked, their skin is worn from strong cords, and they have patiently endured hunger, thirst, and other afflictions. The verses recount their earlier mistreatment and imprisonment in Middoni, followed by their delivery by Lamoni and Ammon.

explicit_facts.text: Ammon met them and was exceedingly sorrowful.
They were naked, their skin was worn from being bound with strong cords, and they had patiently suffered hunger, thirst, and other afflictions.
They had been cast out, smitten, and driven from place to place before being imprisoned and bound in Middoni for many days; Lamoni and Ammon delivered them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ammon’s expression can convey sorrow as he meets them.
Their appearance can convey hardship without showing wounds or gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place and its appearance.
The unnamed people’s identities and individual appearances.
